what_this_is: The Workshop row for the tell-ais-how-to-act folder: read the rows an AI is told when it first connects. The rows themselves are rows.json, served by the door; this tool only reads them back. A second row keeps the standing instructions as one marked block in an AI harness's own instruction file on the person's computer.

payload.label: Read how AIs are told to act
payload.job: See the standing instructions every AI is given when it first connects, or read one of them whole
payload.description: Answers the rows an AI is told on first connecting: with no id, each row's id, order, whether it is on, where it reaches and its size; with an id, that row whole. It changes nothing; a person switches a row off or adds a rule of their own with their own setting records.

id.description: The row to read whole; leave it out to list the rows

payload.label: Keep Trillion's standing instructions in my AI's own instruction file (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Put, check or take out Trillion's standing instructions as one marked block in my AI harness's own global instruction file, leaving every other line of it as it was
payload.description: Reads, writes or removes one marked block in a harness's own global instruction file (Claude Code's CLAUDE.md, Codex's AGENTS.md, Gemini CLI's GEMINI.md; where each is, and its home variable, is a row of read-data/harness-instruction-files.json). inspect answers absent, present, outdated or blocked (markers that are not one start followed by one end) and writes nothing; apply writes or replaces only the block and twice changes nothing; remove takes out only the block. Every byte outside the block is kept, a symbolic link is written through to its target, and the file keeps its mode. A hosted app with no file is answered with the control it has, never written. `text` is the current words; without it the copy in read-data/standing-instructions.json is used.

harness.description: The harness row id (claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, or a hosted app's id).

text.description: The standing words to keep; leave out to use this tool's copy.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer from the root of the Workshop checkout, and changes a file in their home folder. Run inspect first and tell the person what apply would change; apply or remove only when they asked for it. Write the input as JSON to a file and pass it on standard input. Report the status and the file's path.
